requirements.quote:
An UPDATE message is used to advertise feasible routes that share
   common path attributes to a peer, or to withdraw multiple unfeasible
   routes from service (see 3.1).  An UPDATE message MAY simultaneously
   advertise a feasible route and withdraw multiple unfeasible routes
   from service.  The UPDATE message always includes the fixed-size BGP
   header, and also includes the other fields, as shown below (note,
   some of the shown fields may not be present in every UPDATE message):
requirements.condition: When advertising multiple feasible routes in an UPDATE message
requirements.required_behavior: The advertised routes share common path attributes.
requirements.why_checkable: A multi-route UPDATE can be inspected to determine which path attributes apply to its routes.

requirements.quote:
An UPDATE message is used to advertise feasible routes that share
   common path attributes to a peer, or to withdraw multiple unfeasible
   routes from service (see 3.1).  An UPDATE message MAY simultaneously
   advertise a feasible route and withdraw multiple unfeasible routes
   from service.  The UPDATE message always includes the fixed-size BGP
   header, and also includes the other fields, as shown below (note,
   some of the shown fields may not be present in every UPDATE message):
requirements.required_behavior: MAY simultaneously advertise a feasible route and withdraw multiple unfeasible routes from service.
requirements.why_checkable: An UPDATE with both advertisements and withdrawals exercises this permitted combination.

requirements.quote:
An UPDATE message is used to advertise feasible routes that share
   common path attributes to a peer, or to withdraw multiple unfeasible
   routes from service (see 3.1).  An UPDATE message MAY simultaneously
   advertise a feasible route and withdraw multiple unfeasible routes
   from service.  The UPDATE message always includes the fixed-size BGP
   header, and also includes the other fields, as shown below (note,
   some of the shown fields may not be present in every UPDATE message):
requirements.required_behavior: Include the fixed-size BGP header.
requirements.why_checkable: The message encoder and parser can be checked against this field layout.

requirements.condition: For UPDATE message fields that are present
requirements.required_behavior: Order the fields as Withdrawn Routes Length, Withdrawn Routes, Total Path Attribute Length, Path Attributes, then Network Layer Reachability Information.
requirements.why_checkable: The message encoder and parser can be checked against this field layout.

requirements.quote:
This 2-octets unsigned integer indicates the total length of
         the Withdrawn Routes field in octets.  Its value allows the
         length of the Network Layer Reachability Information field to
         be determined, as specified below.
requirements.condition: For the Withdrawn Routes Length field
requirements.required_behavior: Encode the field as a two-octet unsigned integer.
requirements.why_checkable: The message encoder and parser can be checked against this field layout.

requirements.quote:
This 2-octets unsigned integer indicates the total length of
         the Withdrawn Routes field in octets.  Its value allows the
         length of the Network Layer Reachability Information field to
         be determined, as specified below.
requirements.condition: For the Withdrawn Routes Length field
requirements.required_behavior: Set its value to the total length of the Withdrawn Routes field in octets.
requirements.why_checkable: The length value can be compared to the encoded withdrawn-route bytes.

requirements.quote:
A value of 0 indicates that no routes are being withdrawn from
         service, and that the WITHDRAWN ROUTES field is not present in
         this UPDATE message.
requirements.condition: When Withdrawn Routes Length equals zero
requirements.required_behavior: Treat the UPDATE as withdrawing no routes.
requirements.why_checkable: Zero-length withdrawal handling can be checked for absence of route withdrawals.

requirements.quote:
A value of 0 indicates that no routes are being withdrawn from
         service, and that the WITHDRAWN ROUTES field is not present in
         this UPDATE message.
requirements.condition: When Withdrawn Routes Length equals zero
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Include a Withdrawn Routes field in the UPDATE message.
requirements.why_checkable: The message encoder and parser can be checked against this field layout.

requirements.quote:
This is a variable-length field that contains a list of IP
         address prefixes for the routes that are being withdrawn from
         service.  Each IP address prefix is encoded as a 2-tuple of the
         form <length, prefix>, whose fields are described below:
requirements.condition: When a Withdrawn Routes field is present
requirements.required_behavior: Represent the withdrawn routes as a variable-length list of IP address prefixes.
requirements.why_checkable: Decoded list entries can be compared with routes selected for withdrawal.

requirements.quote:
This is a variable-length field that contains a list of IP
         address prefixes for the routes that are being withdrawn from
         service.  Each IP address prefix is encoded as a 2-tuple of the
         form <length, prefix>, whose fields are described below:
requirements.condition: For each IP address prefix in Withdrawn Routes
requirements.required_behavior: Encode an ordered tuple of length followed by prefix.
requirements.why_checkable: The message encoder and parser can be checked against this field layout.

requirements.required_behavior: Encode its Length field in one octet.
requirements.why_checkable: The message encoder and parser can be checked against this field layout.

requirements.quote:
The Length field indicates the length in bits of the IP
            address prefix.  A length of zero indicates a prefix that
            matches all IP addresses (with prefix, itself, of zero
            octets).
requirements.required_behavior: Interpret Length as the IP address prefix length in bits.
requirements.why_checkable: Decoded prefix lengths can be compared to the Length field value.

requirements.quote:
The Length field indicates the length in bits of the IP
            address prefix.  A length of zero indicates a prefix that
            matches all IP addresses (with prefix, itself, of zero
            octets).
requirements.condition: When a withdrawn-route tuple has Length zero
requirements.required_behavior: Interpret the prefix as matching all IP addresses.
requirements.why_checkable: The zero-length prefix match operation can be checked with arbitrary IP addresses.

requirements.quote:
The Length field indicates the length in bits of the IP
            address prefix.  A length of zero indicates a prefix that
            matches all IP addresses (with prefix, itself, of zero
            octets).
requirements.condition: When a withdrawn-route tuple has Length zero
requirements.required_behavior: Encode the Prefix field in zero octets.
requirements.why_checkable: The message encoder and parser can be checked against this field layout.

requirements.quote:
The Prefix field contains an IP address prefix, followed by
            the minimum number of trailing bits needed to make the end
            of the field fall on an octet boundary.  Note that the value
            of trailing bits is irrelevant.
requirements.required_behavior: Include the IP address prefix followed by only the minimum trailing bits needed to end on an octet boundary.
requirements.why_checkable: The message encoder and parser can be checked against this field layout.

requirements.quote:
The Prefix field contains an IP address prefix, followed by
            the minimum number of trailing bits needed to make the end
            of the field fall on an octet boundary.  Note that the value
            of trailing bits is irrelevant.
requirements.condition: When interpreting a withdrawn-route Prefix field
requirements.required_behavior: Ignore the values of the trailing bits used for octet alignment.
requirements.why_checkable: Changing only unused trailing bits must not change the interpreted prefix.

requirements.quote:
This 2-octet unsigned integer indicates the total length of the
         Path Attributes field in octets.  Its value allows the length
         of the Network Layer Reachability field to be determined as
         specified below.
requirements.condition: For the Total Path Attribute Length field
requirements.required_behavior: Encode the field as a two-octet unsigned integer.
requirements.why_checkable: The message encoder and parser can be checked against this field layout.

requirements.quote:
This 2-octet unsigned integer indicates the total length of the
         Path Attributes field in octets.  Its value allows the length
         of the Network Layer Reachability field to be determined as
         specified below.
requirements.condition: For the Total Path Attribute Length field
requirements.required_behavior: Set its value to the total length of the Path Attributes field in octets.
requirements.why_checkable: The length value can be compared to the encoded path-attribute bytes.

requirements.quote:
A value of 0 indicates that neither the Network Layer
         Reachability Information field nor the Path Attribute field is
         present in this UPDATE message.
requirements.condition: When Total Path Attribute Length equals zero
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Include a Network Layer Reachability Information field in the UPDATE message.
requirements.why_checkable: The message encoder and parser can be checked against this field layout.

requirements.quote:
A value of 0 indicates that neither the Network Layer
         Reachability Information field nor the Path Attribute field is
         present in this UPDATE message.
requirements.condition: When Total Path Attribute Length equals zero
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Include a Path Attribute field in the UPDATE message.
requirements.why_checkable: The message encoder and parser can be checked against this field layout.

requirements.quote:
A variable-length sequence of path attributes is present in
         every UPDATE message, except for an UPDATE message that carries
         only the withdrawn routes.  Each path attribute is a triple
         <attribute type, attribute length, attribute value> of variable
         length.
requirements.condition: For every UPDATE message except one that carries only withdrawn routes
requirements.required_behavior: Include a variable-length sequence of path attributes.
requirements.why_checkable: The message encoder and parser can be checked against this field layout.

requirements.quote:
A variable-length sequence of path attributes is present in
         every UPDATE message, except for an UPDATE message that carries
         only the withdrawn routes.  Each path attribute is a triple
         <attribute type, attribute length, attribute value> of variable
         length.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode a variable-length triple in the order attribute type, attribute length, attribute value.
requirements.why_checkable: The message encoder and parser can be checked against this field layout.

requirements.quote:
Attribute Type is a two-octet field that consists of the
         Attribute Flags octet, followed by the Attribute Type Code
         octet.
requirements.required_behavior: Use a two-octet field.
requirements.why_checkable: The message encoder and parser can be checked against this field layout.

requirements.quote:
Attribute Type is a two-octet field that consists of the
         Attribute Flags octet, followed by the Attribute Type Code
         octet.
requirements.required_behavior: Place a one-octet Attribute Flags field before a one-octet Attribute Type Code field.
requirements.why_checkable: The message encoder and parser can be checked against this field layout.

requirements.quote:
The high-order bit (bit 0) of the Attribute Flags octet is the
         Optional bit.  It defines whether the attribute is optional (if
         set to 1) or well-known (if set to 0).
requirements.required_behavior: Use the high-order bit, bit 0, as Optional: value 1 means optional; value 0 means well-known.
requirements.why_checkable: Attribute classification can be checked against the high-order flag bit.

requirements.quote:
The second high-order bit (bit 1) of the Attribute Flags octet
         is the Transitive bit.  It defines whether an optional
         attribute is transitive (if set to 1) or non-transitive (if set
         to 0).
requirements.required_behavior: Use the second high-order bit, bit 1, as Transitive: value 1 means transitive; value 0 means non-transitive.
requirements.why_checkable: Optional-attribute propagation classification can be checked against flag bit 1.

requirements.quote:
For well-known attributes, the Transitive bit MUST be set to 1.
         (See Section 5 for a discussion of transitive attributes.)
requirements.required_behavior: MUST set the Transitive bit to 1.
requirements.why_checkable: Flags on encoded well-known attributes can be inspected for the Transitive bit.

requirements.quote:
The third high-order bit (bit 2) of the Attribute Flags octet
         is the Partial bit.  It defines whether the information
         contained in the optional transitive attribute is partial (if
         set to 1) or complete (if set to 0).  For well-known attributes
         and for optional non-transitive attributes, the Partial bit
         MUST be set to 0.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the third high-order bit, bit 2, as Partial: value 1 means partial information; value 0 means complete information.
requirements.why_checkable: The partial-information state can be checked against flag bit 2.

requirements.quote:
The third high-order bit (bit 2) of the Attribute Flags octet
         is the Partial bit.  It defines whether the information
         contained in the optional transitive attribute is partial (if
         set to 1) or complete (if set to 0).  For well-known attributes
         and for optional non-transitive attributes, the Partial bit
         MUST be set to 0.
requirements.required_behavior: MUST set the Partial bit to 0.
requirements.why_checkable: Flags on well-known attributes can be inspected for a clear Partial bit.

requirements.quote:
The third high-order bit (bit 2) of the Attribute Flags octet
         is the Partial bit.  It defines whether the information
         contained in the optional transitive attribute is partial (if
         set to 1) or complete (if set to 0).  For well-known attributes
         and for optional non-transitive attributes, the Partial bit
         MUST be set to 0.
requirements.required_behavior: MUST set the Partial bit to 0.
requirements.why_checkable: Flags on optional non-transitive attributes can be inspected for a clear Partial bit.

requirements.quote:
The fourth high-order bit (bit 3) of the Attribute Flags octet
         is the Extended Length bit.  It defines whether the Attribute
         Length is one octet (if set to 0) or two octets (if set to 1).
requirements.required_behavior: Use the fourth high-order bit, bit 3, as the Extended Length bit.
requirements.why_checkable: The length decoder can be checked for which flag bit selects length width.

requirements.quote:
The fourth high-order bit (bit 3) of the Attribute Flags octet
         is the Extended Length bit.  It defines whether the Attribute
         Length is one octet (if set to 0) or two octets (if set to 1).
requirements.required_behavior: Encode and decode Attribute Length as one octet.
requirements.why_checkable: The message encoder and parser can be checked against this field layout.

requirements.quote:
The fourth high-order bit (bit 3) of the Attribute Flags octet
         is the Extended Length bit.  It defines whether the Attribute
         Length is one octet (if set to 0) or two octets (if set to 1).
requirements.required_behavior: Encode and decode Attribute Length as two octets.
requirements.why_checkable: The message encoder and parser can be checked against this field layout.
